claims.label: Photograph series shows multiple young men wearing maroon shirts alone in the September 10 audience
claims.claim: A series of photographs displayed during the episode depicts multiple young men in maroon shirts standing alone in the Charlie Kirk event audience on September 10.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference photographs with attendee registration, social media, and military records to identify individuals.

claims.label: Video clip shows a man holding only a maroon shirt in the moments after the shooting
claims.claim: A video clip displayed during the episode shows a man fumbling among a group while holding a maroon shirt (not wearing it) in the moments after the shot.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full uncirculated video footage from multiple angles to confirm and identify the individual.

claims.label: Video clip shows David Sprag standing and appearing to cheer after the shot
claims.claim: A video clip displayed during the episode shows David Sprag (James Norman Rawlinson Jr.) standing and appearing to cheer shortly after the gunshot.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference the clip with public statements by Rawlinson and with the FBI interview he claims to have given.

claims.label: Video clip shows David Sprag and a companion standing under umbrellas at the event
claims.claim: A video clip displayed during the episode shows David Sprag and an unidentified companion standing together under umbrellas while Charlie Kirk's event begins.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the second individual and confirm umbrellas' purpose and provenance.

claims.label: James Rawlinson stated on X that he served in the 19th Special Forces and wore a maroon beret
claims.claim: An audio clip from James Rawlinson's X account, played during the episode, contains his claim that he served in the 19th Special Forces and wore a maroon beret.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify Rawlinson's military service record against official DoD / National Guard records.

claims.label: James Rawlinson stated on X that he has spoken to the FBI
claims.claim: The same X audio clip contains Rawlinson's statement that he has already talked to the FBI and that he hopes they are "on our side."
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with FBI 302 forms, voluntary interview logs, or official acknowledgements.

claims.label: James Rawlinson stated on X that no ambulances were present at the event and the rifle sounded like a .22
claims.claim: The X audio clip contains Rawlinson's claim that there were no ambulances at an event like that and that the high-power rifle sounded like a .22.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare against published video, ballistic evidence, and emergency response records.

claims.label: Article identifies Mihail Kogălniceanu air base in Constanta as a Task Force 82 / 82nd Airborne deployment location
claims.claim: An article displayed during the episode identifies Mihail Kogălniceanu air base in Constanta, Romania as a Task Force 82 / joint base location for 82nd Airborne operations.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm article source, date, and unit assignment through DoD public affairs records.

claims.label: A photograph allegedly shows James Rawlinson in Romania in 2023 wearing a maroon beret
claims.claim: A photograph displayed during the episode allegedly shows James Rawlinson in Romania in 2023 wearing a maroon beret, alongside an unidentified individual on the right.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm identity with Rawlinson himself, military photo archives, and contemporaneous deployment records.

claims.label: A 60 Minutes interview of former Mossad agents described Israeli operations as a "Truman Show" production
claims.claim: An audio clip from a 60 Minutes interview of former Mossad agents, played during the episode, includes the description of Israeli operations as a "global production company" running a "Truman Show" with shell companies hiding Israeli involvement.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the full 60 Minutes episode transcript and air date; verify the speakers' identities and former agency affiliation.

claims.label: Frank Turek stated on a podcast that no exit wound was visible on the back of Charlie Kirk's neck
claims.claim: A podcast audio clip of Frank Turek, played during the episode, contains his statement that he did not believe there was an exit wound on the back of Charlie Kirk's neck during the car transport.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare against the official autopsy report and Brian Harpole's prior podcast statements.

claims.label: Frank Turek stated on a podcast that CPR was performed on Charlie Kirk in the car
claims.claim: The same podcast audio clip of Frank Turek contains his statement that he was "sometimes doing CPR" with Charlie "a foot away."
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference against Brian Harpole's prior podcast statements that no CPR was performed and that the focus was on the wound.

claims.label: Erica Kirk was involved in "modeling apartments" for Next Model Management and MC2
claims.claim: During the episode, the host asserts that multiple people with direct knowledge claim Erica Kirk was in charge of modeling apartments for underaged models at Next Model Management and MC2 during the period when those agencies are defendants in trafficking litigation.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain class action complaint, defendant discovery, and corroborate host's named sources under oath.

claims.label: Pending FOIA requests filed by host's team include NSA, DHS/Secret Service/EOP, FBI, and travel logs
claims.claim: The host states the team has filed FOIA requests to the NSA (Erica emotional asset email), DHS/Secret Service/EOP (WAVES entries for Erica), FBI (Kash Patel schedule), and for FBI plane flight logs and Bradley Hansell's travel schedule September 7-10.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify FOIA request submissions via the agencies' tracking portals and any responses.

claims.label: Lance Twiggs is alleged to be the maroon-shirted individual visible in audience footage
claims.claim: During the episode, the host identifies Lance Twiggs as the individual walking in a maroon shirt in audience footage from the same day.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain higher-resolution frame-by-frame comparison and corroborate via independent witnesses.

claims.label: Tyler Robinson was set up by Lance Twiggs and is not the actual shooter
claims.claim: During the episode, the host states her belief, based on evidence presented thus far, that Tyler Robinson did not kill Charlie Kirk and was set up by Lance Twiggs.
claims.investigative_direction: Examine public charging documents, defense filings, Robinson's alibi evidence, and Twiggs's digital footprint.

claims.label: Andrew Kolbenschlag was physically in the Executive Office Building in Washington D.C. while appearing "live" in Arizona on the Charlie Kirk Show
claims.claim: The host states Andrew Kolbenschlag appeared to be live in studio on the Charlie Kirk Show hosting Kash Patel, but was actually pre-recorded and physically located 5 hours away in the Executive Office Building in Washington D.C.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Secret Service visitor logs, EEOB badge access records, and corroborate the Charlie Kirk Show production timeline.
